entities.summary: Friedrich Graf Kleist von Nollendorf (unknown–17 February 1823) was a Prussian field marshal and a prominent figure in Prussian military during the Napoleonic Wars. Born into the old junker family von Kleist, he was granted the title Graf Kleist von Nollendorf from 1814 onwards. Kleist played a significant role in the Battle of Leipzig (1813) and the Battle of Dresden (1813), where he distinguished himself for his bravery and tactical prowess. His military career was marked by his leadership of Prussian forces during the War of the Sixth Coalition (1813–1814) and his participation in the Congress of Vienna (1815). As a member of the Prussian nobility, Kleist was also a patron of the arts, supporting prominent writers and musicians. He died on 17 February 1823, at the age of unknown, leaving behind a legacy as a skilled military commander and a prominent figure in Prussian history. The Battle of Dresden, which Kleist fought and won, remains a pivotal moment in the Napoleonic Wars, marking a turning point in the conflict and paving the way for the defeat of Napoleon. Kleist's military career was shaped by his experiences during the Napoleonic Wars, which had a profound impact on the course of European history. The Congress of Vienna, where Kleist played a significant role, marked the beginning of a new era of European politics, setting the stage for the rise of the Concert of Europe and the balance of power in Europe for decades to come. Kleist's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he was also a patron of the arts, supporting prominent writers and musicians. His contributions to the arts and literature have had a lasting impact on German culture, cementing his place in the pantheon of great German thinkers and artists.
